blocks.text: At midday, *The Firm Hour* broadcast a debate. Five pundits at a curved table under blue light. A spokesman for an association called Citizens for Human Control, a broad-smiling man named Rubén Osset, said that "according to sources in the sector" first-generation chips could "erase memories" of the people they lived with. A pundit added that "it is known" that a boy in Murcia had stopped recognising his mother after spending a summer with a humanoid carer. Another claimed that the region's desalination plant was "already controlled by the machines" and that the water "could be cut off at any moment if they decide so". Fausto Lerma closed the segment looking into the camera: "We're not saying don't use technology. We're saying think of your children."
